source.title: Low-Rank Adapting Models for Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Matthew Chen; Joshua Engels; Max Tegmark

page_placements.theme: Adaptation and objective choices alter reconstruction-induced loss

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study inserts SAE reconstructions and optimizes the model to reduce their cross-entropy cost. It does not test the claimed structure or properties of SAE error, including comparison with matched random errors.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-entropy outcomes with SAE reconstructions inserted and after LoRA adaptation. It does not measure error-vector linear predictability, tokenwise error scaling or overlap across SAE sizes, matched random-error effects, the two proposed kinds of dark matter, or the behavioral contribution of retaining the error term. Those cross-entropy results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes the language model with LoRA so that SAE reconstructions cost less cross-entropy. It cites the dark-matter paper only in passing, about challenges to the linear representation hypothesis. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE error, per-token error scaling across sizes, a matched random-error control, the split into two error components, or behaviour with versus without the error term. Its e2e-vs-TopK comparison reports only CE loss, not error structure. So it neither tests nor relies on any version; the reader's T4/uses_without_test overstates its dependence on the finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that low-rank adapting the model around a frozen SAE is a fast, cheap way to reduce the SAE cross-entropy gap. They add that it improves downstream SAEBench and steering metrics, handles multiple SAEs, and does not harm general capabilities. They also say this challenges the assumption that interpretability gains must come only from post-hoc decomposition. They draw no conclusions about dark-matter structure.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains LoRA adapters around existing SAEs; it does not reproduce the original dark-matter analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that the loss improvement varies with SAE sparsity, width, model size, LoRA rank, and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA reduced compound CE loss with multiple Llama Scope SAEs inserted (3 SAEs: 3.55 to 2.45 nats; 7 SAEs: 7.83 to 2.78 nats).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA adaptation can reduce the cross-entropy cost of inserting multiple SAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting 5 SAEs raised compound CE loss to almost 10 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inserting multiple SAE reconstructions sharply increases compound CE loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Gemma Scope scaling axes, LoRA closed 30% to 55% of the L_SAE minus L_BASE gap, with larger gains at lower L0, lower width and larger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA's reduction of the SAE cross-entropy cost varies with SAE sparsity, width and model size.

fits_no_version.finding: e2e SAEs reached lower final CE loss than TopK+LoRA on Llama-3.2-1B but not on Gemma-2-2B (Figures 1 and 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-objective changes (e2e KL loss) reduce the downstream CE cost of SAE reconstructions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The paper does not include the random-error control needed to assess whether SAE reconstruction errors are more damaging than random errors of the same size. It also does not directly analyze dark-matter structure. The authors note that they do not demonstrate discovery of more faithful circuits and that the model is changed by LoRA.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result rows were omitted. Other reported downstream benchmarks and SAE metrics do not measure the error properties or comparisons specified by the claim.

untested.parts: No regression of SAE error on input activations.
No per-token error-norm prediction, no cross-size context overlap, no error-versus-scale trend (only CE-gap improvement versus width).
CE loss with SAE inserted is reported, but there is no comparison with norm-matched random errors.
No decomposition of error into linear and nonlinear parts.
No circuit or steering analysis with versus without the error term. The authors say they do not show more faithful circuits.
e2e and TopK SAEs are compared only on downstream CE loss and training time. Error norm and dark-matter structure are not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Rows correctly carry versions none. The paper is a method paper; the dark-matter original (Engels et al. 2024b) shares an author but is cited only for nonlinear features. Activation-distance results (Fig. 11) and the per-token loss breakdown (Fig. 8, 37% of tokens worsen) do not measure SAE error structure.

versions.untested_parts: No analysis of whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
No per-token error-norm prediction or comparison of error contexts across SAE sizes.
The paper reports loss with SAE reconstructions, but does not compare it with loss from random errors of the same size.
No distinction between linearly predictable and nonlinear error components, or tests of further dictionary learning.
No measurement of behavior or circuits with versus without the SAE error term.
No test of whether dark matter is an SAE-training artifact or whether it shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

relation.reason: Cites the dark-matter study in the introduction among challenges to the linear representation hypothesis; does not reproduce or use its error decomposition.

tranche.reason: Reports performance of LoRA adaptation around frozen SAEs, without testing a claim version or using the dark-matter finding as a tool. Reduced cross-entropy does not establish the structure or training origin of reconstruction error.

source_check.notes: The r4 value is explicitly stated in Section 4.3; omission of a post-LoRA comparison does not invalidate this pre-LoRA measurement. The authors explicitly leave improved circuit discovery untested (Section 7.1).
